title: Brand-aware motion and elevation token synthesis for dark console
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Goal: create a cohesive token synthesis strategy that ties brand-specific accent palettes to motion scales and elevation layers for the dark console. This ticket covers token definition, component-level overrides for buttons/tables/charts, accessibility checks for contrast under dark surfaces, and runtime-friendly fallback rules for brands that don't provide full token sets.

Scope:
- Define a small set of motion-scale tokens (motion-01..motion-05) that map to duration/easing pairs and are brand-aware (scale with perceived saturation of accent).
- Define synthesized elevation tokens (elev-00..elev-07) for dark mode that combine alpha overlays + shadow lift for supported brands. Provide deterministic mapping from brand anchor colors -> overlay tint and shadow strength.
- Button family: primary/secondary/ghost size/press states must consume the new elevation + motion tokens to produce consistent interactive feedback in dark mode.
- Table & chart surfaces: introduce thin-stroke tokens and chart-grid-opacity tokens adapted for dark backgrounds to preserve legibility without increasing perceived weight.
- Fallback rules: for brands missing elevation anchors, fall back to a neutral overlay algorithm + brand-accent tint at 6% opacity (configurable). Document how to opt into 'brand-lean' and 'brand-strong' synthesis modes.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Token definitions documented in tokens/theming-v2.md with examples for three brand variants (default, muted-brand, vivid-brand).
2) Figma component kit updated: buttons (all sizes), compact table rows, line/area/column charts with new stroke and fill tokens.
3) Design validations for AA contrast across common surface stacks and reduced-motion mode.
4) Implementation guidance for runtime: clear mapping algorithm and cost (number of tokens computed client-side) so eng can implement without heavy runtime joins.

Technical notes / trade-offs:
- We prefer synthesis (algorithmic generation) to an exhaustive brand token table to reduce integration burden for new brands. Trade-off: small differences between synthesized and hand-tuned brand kits; we'll provide override hooks for brand teams to hand-tune if desired.
- Motion tokens must be conservative for accessibility; provide an explicit reduced-motion flag to switch to motion-01 (minimal) across the console.
- Elevation in dark mode favors subtle alpha overlays over heavy hard shadows to avoid ‘floating’ artifacts at low contrast. Some charts may require stronger stroke contrast; expose chart-grid-opacity as an opt-in token for chart components.

Deliverables:
- tokens/theming-v2.md (spec + mapping algorithm)
- Figma: console-theming-v2.fig (updated components)
- PRD snippet for infra: guidance on when to compute tokens server-side vs client-side
- QA checklist + test prompts for visual-regression and contrast tests

Open questions:
- Should synthesized elevation include per-breakpoint adjustments (mobile vs desktop)? (tentative: yes, but keep to two scales: compact & default)
- How to expose interpolation parameters to Redwood Dedicated customers who want exact parity? (opt: export raw algorithm parameters as config file)
